chunks: From him, from Fudayla, from Aban, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who has a debt of a known amount of dirhams due at a specific term; when the term arrived, the one who owed the dirhams did not have them, so he said to him, 'Take from me dinars at the exchange rate of the day.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.بِصَرْفِ الْيَوْمِ: At the exchange rate of the day
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay a debt in a different currency if you don't have the original one?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the permissibility of settling a fixed silver dirham debt with gold dinars when the debtor lacks the original currency, provided the exchange reflects the current market rate (ṣarf al-yawm). In Shia jurisprudence, this is often interpreted as a valid form of *bayʿ al-dayn bi-l-dayn* (debt for debt) or a flexible settlement that avoids the prohibition of *riba* (usury) by anchoring the value to the prevailing spot rate rather than a fixed, potentially exploitative rate. It highlights the practical adaptability of Islamic commercial law in managing liquidity constraints while maintaining fairness.
